baseline: Current dirty tree after unary payload and projection append work; frozen source manifest and baseline.patch. Not bare HEAD.
acceptance: Preserve ordered expression/metadata pairs and structural ownership; reduce allocations for composing prebuilt 8+8 projections. The paired 95% CPU upper bound must not exceed +5% for ConcatAndSelect, including owned extraction and qs.Select copying. SQL and metadata validation run outside timed subcases. No renderer or database speed claim.
baseline_adapter: Both source projections are prebuilt. Baseline extracts right.Expressions and right.Metadata, rebuilds right Columns with a positional zip, then left.With. No caller scratch buffers are supplied in this cold composition lifecycle. Candidate copies paired columns through projection.Concat.
scope: Projection.Concat only. Uniform variadic collection APIs were withdrawn before timing because they weaken required-first argument prevention; query and sparse-patch fixtures were pruned from both measured harnesses. Original broad baseline fixture and binary retained, never timed.
measurement_harness: Identical pruned fixtures except architectureConcat implementation; only BenchmarkArchitectureProjection/{Concat,ConcatAndSelect} measured.
host_load: Parent confirmed all task-owned builds/tests/lint and scratch PostgreSQL stopped for timing; normal desktop activity uncontrolled.
confidence: Geometric mean of paired candidate/baseline log-ratios; Student t 95% interval across 10 pairs, alternating order. Reported absolute ns/op are medians.
result: Both selected cases save 1024 B/op and 3 allocs/op. Concat CPU effect -56.25%, 95% interval -57.79%..-54.66%; ConcatAndSelect -28.14%, interval -29.64%..-26.60%. Gates passed. No samples removed, retries, or additional timing rounds.
limits: One cold 8+8 projection composition workload on one host, with and without subsequent owned extraction and Select construction. No warm renderer, database, retention, large-list scaling, or cross-library performance claim. No diagnostic profiling was needed for this bounded copy-elimination comparison.
